A0245.title: Financial Reconciliation
A0245.definition: Collect order, payment, refund, fulfillment, and settlement records to reconcile amount, status, and fund-flow consistency by transaction.
A0245.description:
Financial reconciliation collects order payable amounts, payment-channel paid amounts, refund amounts, fees, promotional subsidies, shipment status, clearing-and-settlement records, channel receipts, and reconciliation discrepancy lists, then builds matching rules by order ID, payment ID, channel transaction ID, and settlement date. Rules, thresholds, and discrepancy lists can detect mismatches between order and paid amounts, refunds without discount rollback, duplicate settlement, missed settlement, and abnormal low-price transactions. Payment callback anomalies mainly correspond to webhook forgery and event replay, while duplicate settlement, missed settlement, and refunds without discount rollback can fall under clearing and settlement discrepancy arbitrage.

This control detects fund discrepancies caused by payment amount tampering, unauthorized discount purchases, discount stacking arbitrage, and payment callback anomalies, and provides evidence for post-transaction detection and recovery. Implementation should route exception tickets to after-sales review, delayed benefit issuance and recovery, payment-channel inquiry, and discrepancy freezing and compensation recovery workflows, rather than only producing reports without a response loop.
A0245.limitation: Financial reconciliation often has end-of-day or batch delays, so attackers may complete fulfillment, withdrawal, or resale before differences are found. Inconsistent field definitions across orders, payments, refunds, and channel statements can also create false positives or missed findings. Reconciliation detects differences after they occur, so it still needs server-side recalculation, payment inquiry, and idempotency controls to reduce pre-event bypasses.
